verdict.rationale: vLLM itself serves the API surface coding agents use: an OpenAI-compatible server, the Anthropic Messages API, tool calling with auto/required/named tool_choice, reasoning parsers, and streaming. That makes it a plausible agent backend. The evidence never documents or demonstrates actually connecting a coding agent, so coverage of the full story is incomplete. missing for 10: first-party docs or a guide for connecting a specific coding agent, hands-on or independent corroboration of agent workflows succeeding end-to-end, and evidence on tool-calling reliability under agent loops.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect a coding agent to this product as a working backend

citations.quote: OpenAI-compatible API server, plus Anthropic Messages API and gRPC support
vLLM currently supports named function calling, as well as the `auto`, `required` (as of `vllm>=0.8.3`), and `none` options for the `tool_choice` field in the chat completion API.
Includes a drop-in OpenAI-compatible API for instant integration.
